look_here_first: Start with flower size and the leaf node. Prairie penstemon has enormous pale lavender-to-white flowers, usually about 35–55 mm long, and opposite serrate stem leaves that are sessile and often fused across the node. The calyx and inflorescence are glandular-hairy, and the throat is abruptly inflated.

key_traits.label: Identification

lookalikes.differences: Penstemon triflorus: P. triflorus usually has smaller 25–35 mm pink/red flowers; P. cobaea has much larger abruptly inflated pale flowers and broader serrate leaves. Penstemon tenuis: P. tenuis has much smaller 10–14 mm lavender/violet flowers and favors wet alluvial/coastal prairie habitats. Penstemon baccharifolius: P. baccharifolius is a woody-based subshrub with small thick leathery toothed leaves and red tubular flowers from limestone crevices.
